Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei co-founded firm five years ago
Anthropic will be valued at $1.5tn (£1.14tn) when the five-year-old AI firm makes its stock market debut on Thursday, becoming one of the most valuable companies in the world.
The firm behind the chatbot Claude said its shares will be priced at $83 when it lists on the Nasdaq, a tech-focused stock exchange based in New York.
Anthropic's flotation will make it the first US firm focused exclusively on AI to go public. The seven founders, who set the business up in 2021, will become multi-billionaires .
It will also mark a crucial test for the fast-growing industry, which faces questions over whether the huge amounts of money being poured into the technology will pay off.
The firm said earlier this month it would offer its shares for between $70 and $78 each, which valued the company at up to $1.3tn.
But demand for Anthropic's stock debut - commonly referred to as its initial public offering, or IPO - is very high, according to one early investor in the company who spoke to the BBC on condition of anonymity.
They said shares were more than 10 times oversubscribed ahead of the public listing, meaning demand exceeded the number of shares available.
If that turns out to be the case, Anthropic's valuation could quickly blow past its target on Thursday when trading begins.
Leah Bramwell from Canaccord Wealth said demand for the shares had been "well supported across the board" with strong interest from both institutional and retail investors.
She said that "gives comfort that we're not looking at just a sort of retail-driven frenzy into into AI names".
Depending on how strong demand is, Anthropic could exceed the early market valuation of Elon Musk's SpaceX , which went public in June worth at $2.2tn.
However, in the weeks that followed, SpaceX's share price fell sharply .
As it stands, Anthropic will raise more than $68bn from investors and an additional $26bn from share sales to technology firms including Nvidia which has a long track record of funding firms that buy its AI chips.
OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT and Anthropic's biggest AI rival, is expected to go public next year.
Until then, Anthropic will be the only public company in the US that is entirely focused on the technology, or one that was founded and built around AI tools and products. Its scope is different from tech giants like Google and Microsoft that also develop AI but are involved in other tech services.
There is excitement around Anthropic's listing, but also some concern from investors around its ability to generate future revenue and profits
Yang Wang, a principle financial analyst with Counterpoint Research, said the central issue for Anthropic is whether its business "can keep pace" as hundreds of billions of dollars in financial obligations come due in the next couple of years.
"Nevertheless, it is not an everyday occurrence for public investors to gain direct exposure to a frontier-model developer with the potential to shape the next stage of productivity," Wang said.
Anthropic was started by seven former OpenAI employees, led by brother and sister Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei
Dario Amodei has been outspoken in his belief that AI tools may soon be so powerful that they present a threat to human existence.
The company has urged developers to slow the development of AI, arguing that advanced systems could pose "catastrophic" risks to humanity if they are not handled with safeguards.
OpenAI has also voiced similar sentiments and delayed its plans to list on the stock market to address AI safety concerns.
Nonetheless, Anthropic is looking to grow quickly and gain more access to financing through the public markets.
Stock market trading in technology stocks has been volatile in recent weeks following the US midterm elections when Democrats took control of both chambers of Congress.
Investors are worried about tougher regulation of AI, after Democrat candidates opposed the data centres needed by the technology.
Marta Norton, who heads strategy at investment firm Empower, said the decision by Anthropic to go public now, in a time of market volatility, comes down to the simple fact that the company needs access to more money.
"AI is financially demanding," Norton told the BBC. "The public markets open up the financial spigot a little bit more and so the time has come."
But broader anxieties have started to grow about the AI industry's business model, which is reliant on expensive computer chips that are in short supply.
The technology is dependent on controversial data centres and funding such operations require deals with other tech companies.
The US Federal Reserve has expressed concern about the rapid growth of AI-related debt being financed through "complex and opaque" structures, according to minutes from its October meeting to discuss interest rates.
A few Fed members also noted that "AI-related exposures were becoming increasingly concentrated among a small number of firms".
Can Anthropic's record breaking IPO stop the AI bubble bursting?
How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

Trump is stacking the FCC with Republicans, even as the Democrats boycott.
Senate commerce committee Chair Ted Cruz (R-TX) began a meeting Wednesday meant to confirm President Donald Trump’s nominee to the Federal Communications Commission with a lopsided dais. To his right sat all 14 Republican members of the panel, including Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-SD). To his left were about a dozen empty chairs — every Democratic member of the panel was absent.
Cruz said he’d learned the night before that Democrats intended to boycott the vote, though Democrats say they’d repeatedly raised their concerns about advancing a Republican FCC nominee without a Democratic one. “The administration has shown it’s willing to move Democrats,” Cruz said, pointing to Senate votes scheduled on bipartisan pairs of nominations to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Securities and Exchange Commission. And even though the Supreme Court confirmed his power to do so, Cruz said, Trump has not moved to fire any Democrats from the FCC , as he did at the Federal Trade Commission . “This is an ordinary nomination to fill a vacancy previously held by someone in the same party,” Cruz said.
“This is an ordinary nomination to fill a vacancy previously held by someone in the same party”
But in statements and comments to reporters outside the committee room, Democrats said that the process has been far from normal. Senate committees often vote on nominations to historically independent agencies in bipartisan pairs. Confirming Danielle Thumann Severs, senior counsel to FCC Chair Brendan Carr, to become a commissioner at the agency would put the FCC at four total members — three Republicans and one Democrat, Anna Gomez. Gomez’s term has technically expired, though she can remain on the commission through next year unless she’s replaced. But Democrats fear that by confirming a third Republican to the FCC, Trump might finally fire Gomez , because he’d no longer need her present for a quorum to vote on key actions.
Democrats asked for Thumann’s confirmation vote to be withheld until her nomination could be paired with a Democratic nomination. One way to do that would be to renominate Gomez. But so far, the president has not offered any Democratic nominees for the commission. Democrats said they made their concerns clear to Cruz, and added, “This is not a problem we created, but a problem that the White House can solve.” The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
In addition to the procedural concerns, Democrats worry about Thumann’s work as an adviser to Carr, and whether she was truthful about the matters she worked on. In a letter asking Cruz to delay her confirmation vote, Sen. Ben Ray Luján (D-NM) detailed his concerns. At the November 10th hearing where Thumann answered committee members’ questions, she testified that she had “not worked with the Chairman on any media-related issues,” Luján noted in the letter. But documents obtained via a Freedom of Information Act request show that Thumann was “looped in” on various media matters, and “helped draft Skydance’s commitments that facilitated the 2 FCC’s approval of the Skydance-Paramount merger,” Luján wrote. “She also played a role in processing informal complaints related to CBS 60 Minutes alleged news distortion and she apparently orchestrated the Commission’s response to consumers regarding the Jimmy Kimmel controversy.” The FCC did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the matter.
Even Cruz admitted concerns with Carr’s handling of Kimmel’s comments in the aftermath of conservative activist Charlie Kirk’s killing. But at Wednesday’s meeting, he said he “emphatically agree[s]” that Thumann had resolved any lingering worries about that. He added that his JAWBONE Act , which the committee previously passed, could directly address First Amendment violations by government agencies of either party. The bill would let individuals sue government officials if they illegally try to compel social media or broadcast companies to remove their speech. Sen. Jerry Moran (R-KS), who’d similarly expressed concern over the Kimmel incident, said he found Thumann’s responses on the subject “comforting,” including in a phone call earlier that morning where he said he’d expressed his “serious interest in how the FCC protects and promotes free speech, including free speech on broadcast.” On the call, he said, “she was able to satisfy me once again in her answers, including an explanation for her role at the FCC and her lack of engagement on this type of issue as the FCC made decisions.”
“If she was lying about this, what else is she lying about and what else is she hiding?”
Speaking to reporters outside of the hearing room ahead of the meeting, Luján accused Thumann of lying to the committee. “The questions that I have is if she was lying about this, what else is she lying about and what else is she hiding?” he said. Luján said he wants both Thumann and Carr to appear before the committee by the end of the year to answer lawmakers’ questions. Asked if he’d support using the committee’s subpoena power or even pursuing impeachment against Carr when Democrats regain power next year, Luján said his vote to confirm Carr as a commissioner under President Joe Biden is among his biggest regrets, and that while he hopes Carr will testify voluntarily, “everything should be on the table here to be able to get answers for the American people.”
When it came time to vote on whether to advance Thumann’s nomination for a final step of a vote on the Senate floor, all 15 Republicans voted “aye.” That gave Thumann enough votes for her nomination to advance to the Senate floor, where it’s expected to pass along party lines once scheduled. Still, the clerk listed off the names of the 13 Democratic committee members whose seats remained empty. There was no response.

Democrats try to prevent quorum, say Thumann lied about not working on media issues.
A Senate committee chaired by Ted Cruz (R-Texas) voted today to approve a Federal Communications Commission nominee, despite accusations that the nominee gave false testimony about her work as a legal advisor for FCC Chairman Brendan Carr. Democrats attempted to prevent a quorum by not showing up, but Cruz proceeded with a Republican-only vote.
All 15 Republicans on the Senate Commerce Committee voted to approve Trump nominee Danielle Thumann, while the committee’s 13 Democrats were absent. “We’re going to be doing our job today, even if the Democrats refuse to show up to do theirs,” Cruz said at today’s hearing.
Nominees are vetted in committees first, and then seek require majority approval from the Senate. Republicans are hoping to get Thumann confirmed before Democrats take Senate control in January.
Although the Senate Commerce Committee generally requires one minority member to be present for nomination votes, a spokesperson for Cruz said Senate rules allow the nomination to be advanced for a vote in the entire chamber. A spokesperson for Sen. Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.), the top Democrat on the committee, said in response that “since 2005, Commerce Committee rules required that a quorum include one member of the minority for official action on bill, resolution, or nomination.”
Technically, the committee has operated with no rules during Cruz’s chairmanship because Cruz “failed to pass committee rules” for the current session of Congress, Cantwell’s spokesperson said. “Nevertheless, in practice it has operated in line with rules from the last Congress (and this provision, specifically, since 2005), including that a quorum with a member of the minority party must be present for official action on a nomination or legislation. Until today.”
At a hearing last week, Thumann said she never worked with Carr on media-related topics, leading to accusations that she provided false testimony. “I have not worked with the chairman on any media-related issues,” Thumann said after Sen. Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.) asked, “Do you support Chairman Carr’s illegal campaign to remove Jimmy Kimmel from the nation’s airwaves?”
“It appears that Ms. Thumann misled the Committee and offered false testimony, seriously calling into question her judgment and character and impeding the Committee’s work in determining whether she should be seated on the Commission,” Luján wrote in a letter to Cruz yesterday. “While Ms. Thumann testified she did not work ‘on any media-related issues,’ documents obtained through Freedom of Information Act requests demonstrate that she worked on several media-related issues, including on commitments that Skydance made to pave the way for FCC approval of its merger with Paramount.”
The FCC website describes Thumann as senior counsel to Carr on matters before the Wireline Bureau, the Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau, and the Consumer and Governmental Affairs Bureau. Emails obtained in a public records request by the group Protect Democracy show she had some involvement in media-related matters.
Thumann provided follow-up responses to senators’ questions this week. She said that her work sometimes includes “reviewing documents or filings in a matter outside of my designated portfolio. However, I did not have any conversations with Paramount, CBS, or Skydance related to the merger.”
Thumann has been referred to as Thumann Severs in the nomination process, but she uses the name Thumann.
Luján wrote that Thumann “played a role in processing informal complaints related to” alleged news distortion on CBS’s 60 Minutes , and that “she apparently orchestrated the Commission’s response to consumers regarding the Jimmy Kimmel controversy.” However, Thumann was only a recipient of the Kimmel-related emails we found in a search of the messages.
The emails do show that Thumann approved language used in a response the FCC gave to complaints about the alleged news distortion in a 60 Minutes interview with Kamala Harris. The response informed people who submitted complaints that they should instead submit comments on an FCC docket that had been set up for the 60 Minutes proceeding.
“Hi Kristi, I have confirmed with the Chairman and Erin that we would like for complainants to be encouraged to resubmit their news distortion complaints in the relevant ECFS [Electronic Comment Filing System] proceeding,” Thumann wrote. “Can you please work on some draft language to send to consumers that would advise them on this step (including how to use ECFS)?”
Democrats announced yesterday that they would try to prevent a quorum for today’s vote. They objected to adding a third Republican to the committee while a Democratic seat remains empty.
“All Democratic members of the Commerce, Science and Transportation Committee object to the majority stacking independent commissions with Republicans and rushing nominees through the Committee process in this lame duck session with no Democratic pairs,” Cantwell said in a statement.
Cantwell and other Democrats on the committee sent a letter to Cruz urging him to cancel the vote, while quoting his own words from 2014. “As you wrote in 2014, controversial nominees ‘should not be confirmed in the lame duck session of Congress by senators who just lost their seats and are no longer accountable to the voters.’ We agree,” the Democratic committee members said.
Cruz said today that “Democrats will control the Senate, unfortunately, in January. But today is November 18.” Cruz said there is “ample precedent” for advancing nominations in a lame-duck session.
Senate Commerce Committee rules state that a quorum for nomination votes requires a “majority of the members, which includes at least one minority member.” But a Cruz spokesperson pointed to certain clauses regarding committee quorums in Senate rules when contacted by Ars today.
In the Standing Rules of the Senate , paragraph 7 of rule XXVI says that “no measure or matter or recommendation shall be reported from any committee unless a majority of the committee were physically present,” and does not have any requirement for minority members to be present. Elsewhere, the Senate rules say that when a committee reports a measure to the Senate floor, “no point of order shall lie with respect to that measure” as long as the committee took its action “in conformity with the requirements of paragraph 7 of rule XXVI.”
While committees can have different quorum rules, a Cruz spokesperson said this functions as a “cleansing clause” so that “earlier procedural irregularities, such as a violation of a committee rule, cannot be used to invalidate the vote on the Senate floor.”
FCC nominations have traditionally been paired with one Republican and one Democrat when there is an empty seat for each party. But Cruz said that’s not a requirement.
“There’s nothing that requires the president to nominate in pairs… the law merely says that no more than three of the commissioners may be from the same party,” Cruz said during the Republican-only meeting.
The Communications Act prohibits a single party from holding more FCC seats than is necessary to form a majority. It says, “The maximum number of commissioners who may be members of the same political party shall be a number equal to the least number of commissioners which constitutes a majority of the full membership of the Commission.”
Republicans would have a 3-1 majority on the FCC if Thumann is confirmed by the Senate. The sole Democrat, Anna Gomez, would have to leave at the end of 2027 if Trump does not nominate her for another term.
“There is no mandate for the outgoing majority to rush through a partisan FCC nomination in its final weeks… Ms. Thumann Severs’ nomination should be postponed until the next Congress and paired with Commissioner Gomez’s renomination and the nomination of an additional Democratic commissioner,” Democrats told Cruz in their letter this week.

The government doesn’t know what they are going to be used for, but that’s beside the point. Their real purpose is to sustain the share price of big tech
I t should have the status of an economic law: the sectors a government does most to promote in the name of growth are the sectors most likely to tank the economy. In the UK and the US, deregulation was meant to turn the financial sector into a never-ending growth machine. We have not yet fully recovered from the crash it helped cause in 2008. Fossil fuels are the most heavily subsidised sector on Earth. All that public money makes us highly vulnerable to oil price shocks, the whims of autocrats and societal collapse caused by climate breakdown. As for the great growth priority of our time – AI and datacentres – well, don’t take it from me. As Anthropic’s IPO prospectus warns , advanced AI systems could pose “catastrophic or existential risks to humanity”.
One thing we learned from the US midterm elections is that the drive to build datacentres is less a function of real commercial demand than of the need to sustain the share price of the big tech companies. After citizens across the US voted for moratoria on new datacentres, tech stocks , which have become dangerously dominant, plummeted, triggering fears of wider contagion . Whether new datacentres are required or not, we must keep building them, because confidence depends on them, and without that confidence the bubble will pop. The more you build, and the more this value dependency grows, the bigger the bubble becomes.
This could be why, combined with its catastrophic reliance on commercial lobbyists to tell it what to think, the UK government has enabled datacentres to be classified as “nationally significant infrastructure” , allowing them to swerve local planning control and go straight to ministers for approval. This, the government reasons, is because they are critical to future growth. But growth of what? Some good things, to be sure. But also – and perhaps predominantly – of gambling and pornography, which includes paedophiles nudifying children’s images. Reports of this crime have risen by 8,400% in the past two years, and it has doubtless contributed to that infallible measure of public wellbeing, GDP. Other beneficiaries might include shitposters, fascists using algorithms to boost their content and Russian cyber-attackers.
The government has admitted that while it grants critical special dispensation to these datacentres, it doesn’t know what they are going to be used for. But their ostensible purpose is beside the point. Their real purpose is to sustain the growth in tech shares: growth that could trigger economic collapse.
This is why you must do your duty before God and country, by allowing a vast, roaring, windowless box to loom over your home. This is why you must put your objections aside, and let it destroy your landscape and local character, block out the sun by day and flood the night sky with light, suck the water out of your aquifer , shorten your life with pollutants, guzzle energy and accelerate the climate crisis . This is why you must applaud technologies that are likely to destroy your job. Ask not what the tech billionaires can do for you, ask what you can do for the tech billionaires. Who could deny that inflating the bubble is a critical national priority?
Not only are AI companies likely to be overvalued, but datacentres might be overbuilt . It’s possible that one or two companies will win (especially if they locate the holy grail of “recursive self-improvement”), leaving the others sitting on a heap of very expensive and very dead plant. Of course, mere mortals cannot predict which centres are doomed, but the possibility should at least prompt governments to pause while they see how the sector shakes out. Otherwise, we get both landscape blight and decommissioning costs which – if other failed industries are any guide – are likely to fall on the public.
The world might have moved on, but the UK’s growth plans have not . Despite the tsunami of public protest against them, datacentres are still being “turbocharged” by the government, to “make the UK irresistible to AI firms”. At the same time, the war against our irrational desire for pleasant surroundings and good lives that was launched by Keir Starmer continues. I’m told the government is still pushing the regulating for growth bill. It threatens to tear down even more public protections, and to create “regulatory sandboxes” around the UK. These are places where corporations can do things they’re not allowed to do elsewhere. It’s not yet clear whether these sandboxes will include the government’s “AI growth zones”.
Burnham’s government also seems to be pursuing the grim Starmer project of removing the costs cap – established by the Aarhus convention and guaranteed by the European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018 – for people objecting to damaging schemes. Complain, and you could be landed with a life-changing, home-losing bill. This would shut down a vital aspect of public participation and democracy. Why is it happening? Because the government is not listening to us but to the industry: an industry at odds with almost everyone’s aspirations for a decent life.
An investigation by Spotlight on Corruption discovered that between July 2024 and June 2026, government ministers and officials met representatives from 137 businesses – some of them several times – to discuss their policy on datacentres. In the same period they met just two community groups, and no environmental organisations. We also now have an idea of what such commercial interests have been saying. A submission by the Sovereign AI Leadership taskforce, which represents Nvidia, Microsoft, Cisco and similar companies, warns that the government has one year to force new datacentres through before public objections become overwhelming.
Hence the rush to prioritise them over all other concerns, even – as the residents of Brick Lane in London have discovered – over the prime minister’s proclaimed “defining purpose” , social housing. They are likely both to trash our climate budgets and to make impossible demands on our electricity system. When it comes to mistaking corporate priorities for national ones, Burnham’s administration, it seems, is as easily suckered as Starmer’s.
The government has classified climate activists and Palestine protesters as a threat to national security . But the real threat – to our economy, our jobs, our wellbeing, our democracy, our security, our society and our habitable planet – isn’t hard to locate. It occupies the highest offices of state.

I always tell people that the best thing I’ve ever tested for my job here on the WIRED Reviews team is my automatic litter box from Litter-Robot. I recommend that every cat owner invest in an automatic litter box. If they can swing it, the Litter-Robot is the best option. You’ll be able to say goodbye to the days of scooping and unpleasant smells while this nifty machine does the grunt work for you.
Litter-Robot is the OG automatic litter box , and the name itself has become synonymous with the concept. That’s not by accident, as the brand makes incredibly well-made, ergonomic products that make life easier for pet parents everywhere. Along with their famous automatic litter boxes , they also make a sleek automatic pet feeder that I’ve tested (and loved). These gadgets are an investment and can be pricey, but we here at WIRED love the brand so much that we’ve rounded up some of the best Litter-Robot promo codes, coupons, and deals to make these life-changing pet machines more affordable. Because your pet (and you) deserve it.
If you’ve been wanting to upgrade your litter box system or get the perfect splurge gift for a cat parent in your life, be sure to shop the Litter-Robot Black Friday Sale. During the Litter-Robot Black Friday Sale, you’ll find bundles discounted by up to $150, including bestsellers and new products, with everything you need to get started with the new toilet system, including: the Litter-Robot, litter trap mat, cleaner, litter, bags, and more.
One of the best ways to save big without a Litter-Robot promo code is to buy in a bundle . Litter-Robot offers several bundles that include all the essentials you’ll need to get started with your automatic litter box, such as a litter-trapping mat, replacement waste bags, odor eliminators, litter, and more. Bundles are a great way to save money on the purchases you’ll already need to make, without a Litter-Robot coupon. You can get $75 off several bundles, including Litter-Robot 4 models, as well as the newly released Litter-Robot 5 and Litter-Robot EVO models.
I’ve tested well over a dozen automatic litter boxes from different brands, including several from Litter-Robot. The one I keep coming back to is my personal favorite, the Litter-Robot 4 . Even though the 5 is the newest model (I’ve tested it and I’m in the process of writing the review now), I just can’t quit you, Litter-Robot 4! I still think it's one of the best automatic litter boxes you can buy: it has a user-friendly, intuitive connected app that isn’t overcrowded or confusing; the drawer is easy to pull out to remove waste; it has buttons on the top to manually change; and it doesn’t take up a large footprint on the floor. Plus, with a variety of discounted bundles to choose from, you won’t even need a Litter-Robot promo code.
As previously mentioned, I just tested the Litter-Robot 5 Pro, part of Litter-Robot's recently released line of new models. I was seriously impressed with this model, which looks very similar to the Litter-Robot 4 but has a built-in camera to see what’s going on inside and outside the box. The newest model isn’t cheap, but right now the Litter-Robot 5 Pro Insights Bundle is only $999 ($152 off). This bundle includes the newest Litter-Robot 5 Pro with built-in camera, plus a litter-tracking mat and waste drawer liners to get you started. And as an added bonus, Litter-Robot offers a 90-day in-home trial, a one-year warranty, and free shipping to the lower 48.
The Litter-Robot EVO is another newly released model from Litter-Robot, but it’s a more pared-down, basic version that’s streamlined and compact. I personally love the simpler models (hence my paragraph-long love letter to the Litter-Robot 4 above). If you don’t need to watch a camera feed of your cat peeing and pooping, the EVO is a more affordable, basic option that gets the job done efficiently. Right now, the Litter-Robot EVO Starter Bundle is $782 ($50 off) and includes everything you need to get settled with your new auto box, including waste drawer liners, a litter trap mat, a bag of litter, and odor traps to keep things smelling fresh.

If you’ve been outside, at the gym, or on a basketball court, there’s a good chance you’ve seen someone wearing Reeboks. The brand has had its fair share of ups and downs, but it’s riding a wave of increased interest driven by smart business moves, such as a refocus on sports and lifestyle, alongside high-profile collaborations like the Reebok G-Unit G6 50 Cent .
Founded in 1958, Reebok has changed hands and gone through multiple iterations. Most recently, in 2022, Adidas sold Reebok to Authentic Brands Group for over two billion dollars. Since then, it’s reinvigorated its sports lineup, hired Shaquel O’Neal as president of Reebok basketball, and signed numerous professional athletes across basketball, golf, and tennis to the brand.
But what about the shoes? They’re solid. As someone who used to test training and running shoes , I find the Reebok Floatzig and Reebok Nano X series excellent performers for the price—I still wear my Nano X4s whenever I’m strength training. Other standouts include the more lifestyle-oriented Classic and Club lineups.
But given how often you should replace sneakers (hint: every six months), you should always look for a deal when shopping. That’s why I rounded up some of the best Reebok coupons and promo codes below to help you save time and money.
If you’re looking for a great gift or want to up your sneaker game in the new year, be sure to shop the Reebok Black Friday sale for huge savings on top shoe styles and apparel. Use the Reebok promo code SAVE15 to get $15 off orders of $150 or more. It can be used on everything from plain white classic sneakers to Nano X5 Training Shoes.
The more you spend on Reebok’s site, the more potential savings you can get in its Buy More, Save More section . This collection includes over 1,000 shoes and apparel items, including popular styles like the Club and Nano series, so you can probably find something that fits. With the Reebok discount code BMSM at checkout, you get $10 off orders of $100 or more, $20 off $150 orders, and $30 off orders of $200 or more.
Anyone creating a new account on Reebok online or in the Reebok app can get 15% off their first purchase with the Reebok discount code MOVE15 . This Reebok promo code works after you sign up for a new account and verify your email address, and it is applied automatically at checkout if you are using the Reebok app. Standard exclusions apply to select collaboration items and limited-edition sneaker releases, so double-check your order before purchase to make sure you qualify for the Reebok coupon code deal.
This is the best Reebok deal for frequent Reebok shoppers. With an Authentics Membership ($5 a month), you get 10% off all Reebok products and free shipping on all orders. You also get access to early product drops, sale alerts, and birthday rewards. This perk is applied automatically when you’re logged in with Shop Pay at checkout. An Authentics Membership also gives you discounts at other participating brands like Champion, Billabong, Hunter, Ted Baker, and more, so it’s worth considering, especially if you shop multiple brands. This Reebok discount is for online purchases only.
Saving with Reebok is straightforward if you know where to look. Seasonal sales like Back to School or the standard clearance section offer discounts of up to 65%. Combine these with additional savings from an Authentics Membership, which also provides free shipping, as well as Bundle & Save deals, and you can significantly reduce your cart's total without needing a Reebok discount code.
Students, educators (active and retired), military, veterans, first responders, government workers, health care professionals, and nurses can receive 30% off purchases through the Reebok Heroes discount . All groups must verify their status via ID.me at checkout to receive a single-use Reebok discount code.
One of the easiest ways to get a Reebok discount is by reviewing products you’ve already bought. US-based customers can get 15% off select styles after they submit a review. To snag this Reebok deal, you’ll need to take advantage of this 15% Reebok discount within 30 days of receiving the code. After you submit a review, you’ll get a unique, one-time Reebok promo code. You can also only get a code when you purchase directly from the Reebok site. Plus, the offer excludes delivery charges, isn’t eligible on previous purchases, and cannot be combined with other offers and promotions on the same item (unless otherwise stated).
There are times when a Reebok discount code might not work as expected. Make sure your items aren’t excluded from site-wide Reebok promo codes (some sneakers, new releases, and third-party collabs are). Also make sure you’ve entered the Reebok coupon code correctly, confirmed its terms of use and active window, and met any spending requirements.
You can typically apply a discount code in your cart on Reebok online before you hit checkout. Sometimes codes are applied automatically, but it’s always good to double-check that you are applying the best discount code for your shopping cart.
A Reebok discount or coupon code may not work for a few reasons. Some products, such as select new launches, sneakers, and third-party collaborations, are often excluded from discount codes altogether. Others are time-limited and may have expired. Double-check your code before looking elsewhere—it could be a typo.
Reebok offers a coupon code for students, military, teachers, healthcare professionals, and more through its Reebok Heroes discount program. To verify your status, you’ll be prompted to log in to ID.me at checkout to receive your single-use discount code.
Yes, you can stack Reebok discount codes with sale prices and other promotions. Items in seasonal sales and clearance sections can be combined with promo codes and free shipping benefits from an Authentics Membership.
Yes, Reebok offers a discount code for first-time customers placing their first order. To get yours, create a new account on Reebok online or sign up in the Reebok app. After verifying your email address, you can get 15% off your first order with the code MOVE15 . Standard exclusions, such as third-party collaborations, still apply, though.

Lowe’s Home Improvement grew the old-fashioned way, working its way up from a single, small, family-owned North Carolina general store founded in 1921. But the Lowe’s hardware store empire is plenty big these days. A tool-filled Lowe’s superstore is now about as big as a New York City block. The focus is mostly on appliances and tools for the home DIYer, rather than large building contractors. I like to pop in for grill and griddle tools or just some propane. But you can also buy a pre-finished door complete with the frame—or the lumber, sanders, routers, and saws you’d use to make your own door, including the hinges and the wood stain. It’s easy to get lost in the endless aisles if you love the smell of plaster and wood dust, but it’s easier to find the best Lowe’s deals on the website. This roundup includes Lowe’s daily deals, a promo code, and a Lowe's offer code for 40% off appliances, plus info on the Lowe’s rewards program and military discounts.
With winter quickly approaching and temperatures dropping, now is a great time to stay indoors and tackle the home improvement projects and upgrades you’ve been putting off. Shop the Lowe’s Black Friday sale to save on upcoming projects and home upgrades. You’ll find deals on appliances, tools, holiday decorations, grills, bathroom essentials, kitchen upgrades, and more.
With Lowe’s Deals, you can get up to 35% off select major appliances. During this Lowe’s Deals sales period, you can save up to $2,000 when you bundle select KitchenAid appliances and an additional $100 on select Whirlpool and Maytag laundry pairs. Plus, there are hundreds of select and best-selling appliances like refrigerators, dishwashers, microwaves, ranges, freezers, and more.
It’s no secret that kitchen and bathroom remodels are the most costly home improvement projects any homeowner can take on. For those bigger (and much more costly) renovations, Lowe’s is helping you save more the more you spend. This means you can get up to an additional: 10% off when you spend $750-$1,999, 20% off when you spend $2,000-$4,999, and 30% off when you spend over $5,000. This Lowe’s savings on kitchen and bath program is ideal for homeowners doing a complete room reno, potentially saving thousands of dollars over the course of the project.
Lowe’s wants to tell you about its deals, hoping you’ll be tempted to take advantage of them. If you’re a consistent DIY’er, it’s likely worth getting a heads-up on the Lowe’s Deals of the Day , delivered to your phone via text message. These might include drills, snow blowers, and lawn mowers, plus the best package deals on appliances, refrigerators, washers, and dryers. Each of these deals is available for one day only. If you sign up for text messaging about Lowe’s daily deals, you get $5 off a $50 purchase.
One of the easiest ways to save at Lowe’s is to sign up for Lowe's text alerts. When you sign up for text updates, you'll receive a Lowe’s coupon for $5 off your $50 purchase. This offer is for new text subscribers and provides a unique, one-time-use code that’s applicable to in-store or online purchases. Get $5 Off All Lowe’s Orders
If you’re planning major work this year or just like to putter around, it’s probably worth picking up a MyLowe’s Rewards Program membership. Each eligible purchase accrues points that pay out in $5 increments of in-store credit at Lowe’s. Like many loyalty programs, you get more benefits the more you spend at the store, including free shipping on all purchases, including small ones, member-only discounts, and point boosters for better discounts.
There are three membership tiers, depending on what you buy. One large appliance might already qualify you for the highest tier of rewards, at which point you might as well. These are the three tiers, based on the total cost of what you’ve bought at Lowe’s in the past year. Bronze ($0-$499): $35 minimum for free shipping; 1 point per $1 spent. Silver ($500-$1,999): Free shipping; 1.25 points per $1 spent. Gold ($2,000+): Free shipping; 1.5 points per $1 spent.
For contractors, there’s a separate MyLowe’s Pro Rewards Program that offers Lowe’s in-store credit in $1 increments for every 100 points earned. (Points expire in half-yearly increments, on June 30 and December 31.) Benefits include member-only deals, volume discounts, free standard shipping in the contiguous United States, and a 20% paint discount after an annual spend of $3,000 or more. Other benefits include analytics and spend reports, online order quoting, and purchase authorization for specified crew members.
All verified active military, veterans, and military spouses are eligible for a 10% discount on full-price items—meaning items don’t have to be on sale to qualify. This is available through what Lowe’s calls the Everyday Military Discount program. When you enroll, you also get an immediate upgrade to Silver status in the MyLowe’s Rewards program, which means more rewards points per dollar and free shipping on all orders in the contiguous United States.
Get a free Silver status upgrade instantly when you enroll in our Military Discount program and validate through ID.me. MyLowe’s Rewards Silver status members receive free standard shipping (excludes AK and HI) and earn more points per dollar.
Like many big retailers, Lowe’s also has a store credit card with discounts attached. The MyLowe’s Rewards Credit Card offers 5% off qualified purchases, with a whole bunch of asterisks. Specifically, the discount applies after all other discounts and can’t be combined with other programs like contractor bulk discounts, employee discounts, or military discounts. It also doesn’t work on Weber, Miele, or Kichler products. Scroll to the bottom here for APR and exceptions. The smart person signs up during a big purchase: When you sign up and get approved, you get 20% off an in-store purchase (up to $100 off).
Another way to get 5% off items you need regularly is to set up a Lowe’s subscription. This is good for items ranging from cleaning products, air and water filters, lawn care, pet goods, plumbing, and batteries. Shipping is free, and delivery happens automatically.
You may not realize that Lowe’s has a Lowest Price Guarantee policy , which means that if you find a lower price on an identical item, Lowe’s will match the competitor’s price. All you need to do is chat with a Lowe’s employee in-store or call 1-877-465-6937. Plus, the Lowest Price Guarantee includes the price of the item(s) plus shipping or delivery costs.

Cumhurbaşkanı Yardımcısı Cevdet Yılmaz, Taşkent’te “Özbekistan-Türkiye İş Dünyası Yüksek Düzeyli Konsey Toplantısı”nda konuşuyor
ABD Merkez Bankası (Fed), Federal Açık Piyasa Komitesinin (FOMC) 27-28 Ekim'de düzenlenen toplantısına ilişkin tutanakları yayımladı.
Politika faizinin beklentiler doğrultusunda yüzde 3,75-4 aralığında sabit tutulduğu son toplantının tutanakları, neredeyse tüm Fed yetkililerinin gelecek aylarda ilave sıkılaştırma beklediğine işaret etti.
Fed personelinin enflasyon tahmininin eylül toplantısı için hazırlanan tahminle benzerlik gösterdiği aktarılan tutanaklarda, büyüme öngörüsünün ise eylüle kıyasla bir miktar daha güçlü olduğu kaydedildi.
Tutanaklara göre, Fed yetkililerinin çoğu, politika faizinin sabit tutulmasını desteklerken, ilave bilgi toplamanın faydalarına dikkati çekti.
Birkaç yetkili politika sıkılaştırmasında kademeli bir yaklaşımın işletmelere ve hane halklarına daha yüksek faiz oranlarına uyum sağlamaları için zaman tanıyacağını belirtti.
Bazı yetkililer, piyasa fiyatlamalarına yansıyan aralık ayı ve gelecek yılki sıkılaştırma adımlarına yönelik beklentilerin, uygun politika faizi patikasına ilişkin kendi değerlendirmeleriyle genel olarak uyumlu olduğunu ifade etti.
Birkaç yetkili, politika kararını desteklemekle birlikte, bu kararın kıl payı verilmiş olduğunu düşündüklerini kaydetti.
Birçok yetkili, politika faizini sabit tutma kararının, FOMC'nin enflasyonu zamanında yüzde 2'ye indirme taahhüdünde herhangi bir zayıflama anlamına gelmediği mesajının açıkça verilmesinin önemini vurguladı.
Yetkililerden bazıları, enflasyonun aşırı yüksek seyretmeye devam ettiğini ve hız kestiğine dair çok az işaret gördüklerini vurgulayarak ekim toplantısında hedef aralığın 25 baz puan artırılmasından yana görüş bildirdi.
Mevcut politika duruşunun yeterince sıkı olmadığı değerlendirmesinde bulunan yetkililerden birkaçı, daha fazla gecikmenin yüksek enflasyonun kalıcı hale gelmesi veya ileride daha büyük ve daha sarsıcı bir sıkılaştırmayı zorunlu kılması riskini doğurduğu uyarısında bulundu.
Politika faizinin artırılmasından yana olan birkaç yetkili, ilave sıkılaştırmanın muhtemel olduğunun piyasa katılımcıları tarafından açıkça anlaşılması koşuluyla federal fon oranının sabit tutulmasını destekleyebileceklerini söyledi.
"Önümüzdeki aylara ilişkin para politikası görünümüyle ilgili olarak yetkililerin neredeyse tamamı, enflasyon ve iş gücü piyasasına yönelik temel görünümleri çerçevesinde, enflasyonun yüzde 2 hedefine zamanında dönmesini sağlamak amacıyla, federal fon oranı hedef aralığını artırmaya yönelik ilave adımların muhtemelen uygun olacağı değerlendirmesinde bulundu. Birkaç yetkili, gelen enflasyon verilerinin olumsuz olması halinde bir sonraki toplantıda 25 baz puandan daha fazla bir artışın değerlendirilebileceğini belirtti."
Birkaç yetkili, enflasyonun beklenenden daha kalıcı olabileceğini ve bu durumda daha sıkı bir politika duruşuna geçilmesinin gerekebileceğini gözlemledi.

Bu haberde bir hata mı var? Her türlü talep, şikâyet ve görüş için okur temsilcimize ulaşabilirsiniz.

Defense secretary asserts US dominance on trip that would have seemed ‘impossible, almost unbelievable’ a year ago
Pete Hegseth has used his first visit to Venezuela since US special forces abducted its former president, Nicolás Maduro , to boast of the dictator’s capture during what he called “the single most sophisticated military operation in the history of Latin America”.
Maduro was controversially seized by Delta Force operatives in the early hours of 3 January, setting in motion an improbable rapprochement between Washington and Venezuela’s anti-imperialist “Chavista” regime, which has ruled since 1999.
Speaking outside the recently reopened US embassy in Venezuela’s capital, Caracas, on Wednesday, Hegseth said: “It’s a great honor to be here as the first United States secretary of war this century to set foot in Venezuela.​ Just one year ago my presence here … would have been deemed impossible, almost unimaginable.
“In fact, exactly one year ago today … [Maduro] stood on a stage not too far from here and yelled mockingly, ‘Come and get me!’” Hegseth recalled, before adding sarcastically: “Well, we answered that call.
“The reality is that … January 3 is the day that will go down in history as a day of liberation for Venezuela,” Hegseth claimed, although Maduro’s allies continue to hold power with US support.
Earlier in the day, Hegseth was welcomed to the Miraflores Palace by Maduro’s former vice-president, Delcy Rodríguez , who became acting president with Donald Trump’s blessing after his abduction.
In the aftermath of the deadly US attack, Hegseth was one of the bluntest Trump administration voices when it came to celebrating the invasion. “Maduro had his chance … he effed around and he found out,” the defense secretary bragged .
Speaking at the palace, Hegseth struck a more conciliatory tone as he vowed to deepen cooperation with Venezuela’s new leaders in brief comments that were broadcast by the state broadcaster VTV.
“I stand here on behalf of President Trump, who sends his greeting and looks forward to the opportunities, not just militarily … but also economically: the incredible resource capabilities that your country has, that we look forward to unlocking together with you,” Hegseth told Rodríguez and senior cabinet members, including the defense and foreign ministers, Gustavo González López and Oliver Blanco.
Hegseth said his visit to Rodríguez’s “beautiful country” was designed to re-establish and increase “defense cooperation” between “two great militaries” that less than a year ago were briefly at war. Earlier this month, the New York Times reported that Trump officials were trying to negotiate a long-term US troop presence in Venezuela as part of their push for regional hegemony.
“I appreciate your leadership and commitment to your country,” Hegseth told Maduro’s successor, a once outspoken anti-imperialist leftist who has overseen an unlikely realignment with Washington since her ally was grabbed.
During her five-minute address, Rodríguez, whose oil-rich country is widely seen to have become a US protectorate after January’s invasion, made no mention of Maduro, who is behind bars in New York City.
But referring indirectly to his capture and the subsequent reconciliation with Washington, she told Hegseth: “Thanks to the political and geopolitical maturity of our governments, we have – in a very short period of time, just a few months – turned what were very difficult and very tough times for our people, into an extraordinary space for cooperation and mutual benefit.”
Rodríguez hailed the “historic” energy deal her government recently struck with Trump, who has called it “the biggest oil deal in world history” as well as “the spoils” of his “conquest” of Venezuela.
Hegseth claimed the agreement, which reportedly involves 65bn barrels of reserves, “makes the strait of Hormuz a non-factor for the western hemisphere”.
Critics of Rodríguez’s political movement painted Hegseth’s visit as a humiliating act of genuflection for a president with no choice but to roll out the red carpet for the man whose troops captured her boss.
Writing on X, Luz Mely Reyes, a prominent Venezuelan journalist, said Hegseth’s visit was designed to underscore Washington’s “direct administration” of her country.
“Ten months after Nicolás Maduro’s capture, Washington no longer needs to fire shots to remind everyone who is in charge: the mere presence on Venezuelan soil of the architect of the January incursion reaffirms that the country’s operational sovereignty is subject to the White House’s directives,” Reyes said.
Reyes suspected the visit also carried a message for members of Venezuela’s armed forces. “Domestically, the trip forces the military high command to legitimize the man who directed the extraction of their former commander in chief,” she said. “In this regard, I wonder whether it might be a message of discipline intended to prevent any pockets of resistance in the barracks.”
Trump’s attempts to expand his Shield of the Americas anti-cartel coalition of Latin American governments suffered a major blow last month with the defeat of his far-right ally, Flávio Bolsonaro, in Brazil’s presidential election. The leftwing winner, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has indicated his country will not join the initiative.
But Venezuela’s interim government is in little position to resist. During his surprise visit to Venezuela, Hegseth said Venezuela had gone from being “our most aggressive regional threat to [being] a compliant security partner”. He praised Rodríguez for working “closely, pragmatically, and diligently with the United States to stabilize Venezuela”. Hegseth claimed US and Venezuelan armed forces would work together to attack “narco-terrorists” operating on Venezuelan soil, vowing: “We will hunt you down. We will find you. And we will kill you.”
Concluding her speech at the palace, Rodríguez told her foe-turned-friend: “Thank you, secretary, and I wish you a lifetime of happiness.”

texts.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cw8r:
Residents fled the area near Nuseirat and Bureij refugee camps following the Israeli evacuation order
Israeli ground forces have launched a rare operation in part of the central Gaza Strip outside their control, after issuing evacuation orders for residents.
Witnesses said tanks advanced east of Nuseirat refugee camp and rolled onto the territory's main north to south road under the cover of artillery strikes.
The Israeli military said the "targeted" operation aimed to dismantle a "terror tunnel" west of the so-called Yellow Line, which marks the more than 60% of Gaza's territory occupied by Israel.
The Palestinian armed group Hamas, which controls the rest of Gaza, accused Israel of a "flagrant violation" of the October 2025 ceasefire agreement.
Violence has continued in Gaza over the past 13 months, with near-daily Israeli strikes, and living conditions for the 2.1 million people there remain dire.
Early on Wednesday afternoon, Israeli military body Cogat's Arabic spokesperson announced the start of the incursion and warned Palestinians living in an area north of Nuseirat and Bureij refugee camp to stay away for their own safety.
It also said a section of the north to south Salah al-Din road that passed through the area would be closed to traffic.
Later, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said it had begun a joint operation with the Shin Bet security service "to dismantle a terror tunnel west of the Yellow Line that posed an immediate and direct threat to IDF troops".
"IDF troops under the Southern Command are deployed in the area in accordance with the ceasefire agreement and will continue to operate to remove any immediate threat and thwart attempts by the Hamas terrorist organisation to harm Israeli civilians or IDF troops, or to violate the agreement," it added.
Hamas warned in a statement that the advance of Israeli military vehicles beyond the Yellow Line and the evacuation of residents constituted "a dangerous development and a flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement".
Footage published by Palestinian media outlets and on social media showed families fleeing areas near Nuseirat camp following the announcement.
In one video verified by BBC Verify, a man can be seen ducking after hearing artillery fire and then running along Salah al-Din road, about 1.5km (0.9 miles) west of the Yellow Line. "The Israeli occupation now is firing randomly near the houses and tents of people," he says.
Automatic gunfire can be heard in another video filmed just to the south-east.
A resident of Nuseirat who was forced to flee told BBC Arabic's Middle East Daily programme: "The situation is now extremely dire, with Israeli forces firing indiscriminately at areas where displaced people have sought shelter."
"We couldn't take any of our belongings with us - not even our blankets, pillows, or clothes. We had no choice but to leave everything behind."
A second resident also reported "indiscriminate gunfire and shelling" and said there had been "numerous casualties, including fatalities".
Asked about reported fatalities, the IDF sent a general statement about the operation.
Israel building new land barriers in Gaza and displacing families
Israel moves Yellow Line deeper into Gaza, satellite images show
Gaza's Hamas-run Civil Defence agency said three people were killed and others were wounded in three separate Israeli drone strikes on Wednesday.
One man was killed in Nuseirat, the second to the north in Gaza City, and the third in the central town of Deir al-Balah, it added.
The IDF told the BBC that it had "struck several military operatives".
At least 1,658 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza since the ceasefire began last year, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.
The Israeli military says six of its soldiers have been killed over the same period.
Meanwhile, more than 1.9 million people - about 90% of Gaza's population - remain displaced, with 1.4 million of them living in tents or makeshift shelters, according to the UN.
Reconstruction has yet to begin in Gaza, where an estimated 82% of all structures have been destroyed or damaged during the war, as US President Donald Trump's peace plan has largely stalled.
The group has agreed to give up its weapons in exchange for a phased withdrawal of Israeli troops from the 60% of Gaza they currently occupy. But Israel has insisted that Hamas must fully disarm before any pullout.
The war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.
Since then, more than 74,700 people have been killed in Gaza, the health ministry says.

The US, Chinese and Russian leaders are to hold their first three-way talks on the sidelines of the APEC summit.
US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin will hold a three-way meeting on Thursday in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen, the first ever between the leaders of the world’s three most powerful militaries.
The meeting, which will take place on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, has drawn comparisons with the 1945 wartime Yalta conference at which the United States, United Kingdom and then-Soviet Union agreed on the post-war order. But those powers had been allied during a world war. Analysts say the three men meeting on Thursday are arriving with very different goals, and that few concrete outcomes can be expected.
“It’s a summit of Trump’s ego, Putin’s tactics, China’s strategy,” Scott Lucas, professor of international politics at University College Dublin, told Al Jazeera.
The trilateral meeting is taking place on the sidelines of the APEC leaders’ summit, which China is hosting in Shenzhen on November 18 and 19. Trump travelled to China after attending the Association of Southeast Asian Nations ( ASEAN ) meeting in Manila.
The White House has said that Trump plans to discuss the war with Iran as well as a possible three-way agreement on nuclear armament with Xi and Putin. Ukraine is not expected to be on the formal agenda, as Xi is understood to be reluctant to be drawn into what he views as a European matter.
The meeting comes as Trump has strained ties with traditional US allies, at times floating troop withdrawals from South Korea and cuts to assistance for Japan, while his administration continues to describe China as Washington’s main geopolitical rival.
Vuk Vuksanovic, a lecturer in foreign policy and grand strategy at the Department of War Studies, King’s College, London, cautioned against viewing the summit as a new “carve-up” of the world order, however.
“It is a far cry from being a new Yalta,” he said. “In Yalta, you actually had the idea about how the world was going to look, and where the demarcation line would potentially be between the superpowers. We don’t have anything similar, not even the contours of that, in the making at this moment.”
At the Yalta Conference in February 1945, US President Franklin D Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill and Soviet leader Joseph Stalin met in Crimea to shape the post-war order, agreeing on the division of Germany and setting the stage for Soviet influence over Eastern Europe.
Trump landed in Shenzhen on Wednesday, with Xi greeting him at the airport. This is their third in-person meeting since they paused their bitter trade war late last year. At its height, US trade tariffs on Chinese goods reached 145 percent, with China retaliating with tariffs of 125 percent on US goods, before a temporary truce agreed in Busan, South Korea, in October 2025, when tariffs were relaxed. Xi also agreed to pause new restrictions on exports of some rare earth metals which are crucial for manufacturing technology from smartphones to fighter jets. Soon after that, Trump relaxed restrictions on the sale of some Nvidia AI-related computer chips to China.
The truce has since been extended to January 10, 2027 to allow for broader trade talks.
China’s rare earth mineral exports to the US are still about 75 percent below normal levels, according to the Center for Strategic and International Studies.
A scandal over Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data centre company accused of diverting Nvidia chips to China in breach of US export controls, has also strained ties, as has the recent scandal over Nvidia’s former CEO, Jensen Huang’s extramarital affairs, including with a woman the US has accused of spying for China.
Beijing rejects all spying allegations as “baseless”, and Trump has said he does not plan to raise the issue at this meeting.
Expectations are low for a major thawing, however: Deborah Elms, head of trade policy at the Hinrich Foundation, told Al Jazeera that a handshake without incident would be seen as a win.
Trump’s special envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, have brokered talks between Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11, the first in direct format since February. The pair have visited both Kyiv and Moscow to promote these talks in recent days.
Days before they travelled to Moscow on Thursday last week, Trump said Washington and Moscow were close to a “big, beautiful agreement” covering not just Ukraine but “all of Europe”.
Trump’s rhetoric towards Putin has softened greatly in recent months, as it has hardened against Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, whom he has publicly admonished for targeting Russian energy facilities, driving up the global cost of oil and diesel. Trump has also called for Zelenskyy to step down and has paused some sanctions on Russian oil, much to the anger of many in his Republican Party .
Some analysts are concerned that US negotiators may offer Russia concessions on NATO in return for peace, including pushing a deal that allows Russia to retain land it has seized from Ukraine in the past four years – a prospect that alarms European leaders.
China has become Russia’s top trading partner since Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, weeks after the two had declared a “no limits” partnership.
At a summit in Beijing in May this year, Xi and Putin signed more than 40 cooperation agreements and hailed growing energy trade.
Russian oil exports to China rose 35 percent in the first quarter of 2026, according to a Kremlin aide. China has also ignored Western demands to stop supplying high-tech components to Russia’s weapons industry.
Chinese President Xi Jinping called for China and Russia to “lead and advance the trend towards a multipolar world” after holding talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.
Putin addressed the summit after Xi. He described Western powers as “former hegemons” and said Europe was experiencing a “humiliating decline”.
Analysts say Trump is the leader most eager to walk away with something he can present as a “win” from this trilateral meeting.
Vuksanovic said Trump is arriving “wounded domestically” following his Republican Party’s crushing defeat at the US midterm elections, which have seen the Democratic Party gain control of both US Houses of Congress. Trump’s legacy, Vuksanovic added, has been damaged by the war on Iran, particularly in light of Trump’s pledge not to drag the US into another “forever war” during his presidential campaign in 2024.
The deadlock that currently exists between the US and Iran has been described as a “ frozen war ” by observers.
“[Trump] hopes that he can get some quick-fix deal on something, at least, which he can then try to spin and sell to his base in the US as an enormous accomplishment,” Vuksanovic said. But he added that he doubts Trump could secure anything beyond “something very symbolic”, noting that the agenda of the meeting has remained opaque.
One issue Trump may push for is a trilateral agreement on nuclear armament. The New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty (New START) between Russia and the US lapsed in February. It was first signed in 2010 and caps US and Russian strategic nuclear arsenals.
Trump previously rejected Russia’s proposal to extend the treaty after it expired, demanding instead a “new, improved and modernised” deal that includes Beijing. However, Xi is understood to be unenthusiastic about joining a treaty that China had no part in writing.
Lucas said Trump is there largely “for the photo opportunity”. But he drew a distinction between Trump and his administration, which he said wants to “regain their footing a little bit in terms of leadership” on China.
Washington’s China policy, Lucas said, has been “a disaster”. The administration launched a tariff war that saw duties climb as high …

texts.https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n:
First incursion across boundary since ceasefire deal comes as Eisenkot seeks to form government without Netanyahu
The Israeli military crossed into Hamas-controlled central Gaza on Wednesday in its first ground operation across the “yellow line” boundary since a fragile ceasefire was agreed last October, forcing dozens of displaced Palestinians to flee their tents.
Israeli tanks rolled along the Salah al-Din road , Gaza’s main north-south route, a day after the US-backed Board of Peace, a body overseeing the ceasefire, accused Israel and Hamas of failing to honour their commitments to end hostilities.
An Israeli military spokesperson said troops were carrying out an operation targeting “Hamas infrastructure” west of the yellow line in central Gaza .
The military ​has not commented extensively on the operation, which came as the Israeli opposition politician, Gadi Eisenkot, has been seeking to form a government without the caretaker prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, who has built his political reputation on promises to keep Israel safe.
A Gaza security source told AFP there was “intense Israeli artillery shelling” north of Nuseirat refugee camp and reported Israeli military vehicles in central Gaza “amid ongoing gunfire and airstrikes since midday”.
Hamas condemned the Israeli raid and the forced displacement of Palestinians as “a flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement” and a dangerous escalation. The Israeli military did not immediately respond to Hamas’s statement.
Residents reported hearing tank fire in the area. Palestinian medics said one person was killed in an Israeli airstrike near the site of the raid.
In separate incidents on Wednesday, Palestinian medics said two people were killed by Israeli fire, one in Deir al-Balah and the other in Gaza City. The Israeli military said it was unaware of any incident in Deir al-Balah and had struck a militant in Gaza City.
Israel has stepped up its attacks on Hamas, which it says has been regrouping and rearming. Hamas has accused Israel of trying to derail the US-brokered ceasefire agreed in October 2025.
Israeli strikes have continued since the ceasefire, and Hamas remains armed.
Last week, an Israeli airstrike on Nasser hospital in southern Gaza killed six people, including a surgeon and a disabled man, and wounded 28 others, according to the hospital director.
The body overseeing Donald Trump’s plan to end the war in Gaza has accused Israel and Hamas of failing to honour their commitments to end hostilities, leaving Palestinians in dire conditions and the ceasefire at risk of collapse.
In its second report to the UN security council since the truce began 13 months ago, the Trump-led Board of Peace said the gap between what was agreed and what was happening on the ground remained the biggest threat to the deal. The report, seen by Reuters, warned that “a ceasefire that delivers nothing visible cannot be sustained indefinitely”.
Gaza’s health authorities say at least 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire came into effect. The Israeli military says five of its soldiers have been killed over the same period.
Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed in Gaza since Israel launched its military campaign in response to the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, in which about 1,200 people were killed.

Dün yayımlanan Fed Açık Piyasa Komitesi (FOMC) toplantı tutanaklarında enflasyonun yüzde 2 hedefine dönmesi konusunda ilave faiz artışlarının muhtemelen uygun olacağı görüşü öne çıktı. Bazı üyelerin, enflasyon verilerinin tahminleri aşması durumunda aralıkta 25 baz puandan daha büyük bir artışın değerlendirilebileceği görüşünde olduğu tutanaklarda yer aldı. Ayrıca yapay zeka yatırımları, tutanaklarda tartışma konusu olurken, hem enflasyonun hem de potansiyel finansal istikrarsızlığın bir tetikleyicisi olarak görüldü.
Fed tutanakları, bankanın gelecek dönemde faiz artışlarını sürdürebileceğine ilişkin beklentileri pekiştirdi. Para piyasalarındaki fiyatlamalarda, Fed'in aralık toplantısından başlayarak 4 toplantının 3'ünde politika faizini artırabileceği olasılığı güç kazandı.
Para politikalarında ilave sıkılaşma beklentileriyle dolar, diğer para birimleri karşısında değerlenmeye devam etti. Dolar endeksi 104 seviyesine yaklaşarak Nisan 2025'ten bu yana en yüksek seviyeyi gördü.
Fed yetkililerinin açıklamaları da izlenirken, Fed Yönetim Kurulu Üyesi Christopher Waller, enflasyonla mücadele için agresif adımlar atılması gerektiğini belirterek, fiyatların beklentilerinin üzerinde artmaya devam etmesi nedeniyle merkez bankasının "insanları şaşırtması" gerektiğini ifade etti.
Fed Yönetim Kurulu Üyesi Michael Barr da enflasyon baskılarının devam ettiği ekonomide daha sıkı para politikasını destekleme eğiliminde olduğunu belirtti. Barr, "Ekonomi şu anda öngördüğüm şekilde gelişirse faiz oranlarının daha da artırılmasının uygun olacağını düşünüyorum." ifadelerini kullandı.
San Francisco Fed Başkanı Mary Daly ise faiz oranlarının daha da artırılması gerektiğini ancak Fed'in ekonominin nasıl şekillendiğini değerlendirirken para politikasını sıkılaştırma konusunda ölçülü bir yaklaşım benimsemesi gerektiğini kaydetti. Daly, "Enflasyonun yüzde 2'ye doğru kademeli bir düşüş eğiliminde olduğundan tamamen emin olabileceğimiz bir noktaya ulaşmak için faiz oranlarını daha da artırmamız gerekecek." değerlendirmesinde bulundu.
Öte yandan ABD’de petrol ve benzin stokları beklentilerin üzerinde artarken, akaryakıt fiyatları ise gerilemeyi sürdürdü. Benzin stokları 1,6 milyon varillik artış beklentisine karşın 5,2 milyon varil artarak 215,9 milyon varile ulaştı.
Bu gelişmeyle Batı Teksas türü (WTI) ham petrolün varil fiyatı spot piyasada yüzde 3 düşüşle 81,8 dolara indi. Küresel arzın genişlemesiyle Brent petrolun varili de 31 Ağustos'tan bu yana ilk kez 90 doların altında günü tamamladı.
Analistler, petrol ve akaryakıt fiyatlarındaki düşüşün küresel enflasyon baskılarını hafifletebileceğini ve merkez bankalarının para politikasındaki manevra alanını genişletebileceğini belirtti.
Bunlara ek olarak yapay zeka alanında ABD'li çip üreticisi Nvidia'daki yönetim belirsizliği sürerken, bu etkiler güçlü bilançoya rağmen hissede kalıcı bir yükselişe dönüşmedi. Nvidia hisseleri dün yüzde 2,9 geriledi.
Nvidia'nın bilançosu yapay zeka talebinin sürdüğüne işaret etse de yönetime ilişkin belirsizlikler hissede satış baskısı yaratırken, çip sektöründe hisse bazlı ayrışma ve seçici alımlar öne çıktı. Yapay zekayla ilgili süregelen endişelerin gölgesinde Claude yapay zeka modellerinin geliştiricisi Anthropic'in halka arzı bekleniyor. Şirketten yapılan açıklamada, halka arz kapsamında hisse başına 83 dolardan 980 milyon adet hissenin satışa sunulduğu bildirildi.
Böylelikle halka arzın büyüklüğü 81,3 milyar dolar olarak hesaplanırken, Anthropic, SpaceX'i geride bırakarak tüm zamanların en büyük halka arzına imza attı. Haziran ayında borsaya açılan SpaceX, halka arzında ek hisse alım opsiyonu hariç 75 milyar dolar kaynak toplamıştı.
Açıklamada, şirketin hisselerinin bugün Nasdaq borsasında "ANT" koduyla işlem görmeye başlamasının beklendiği, halka arz işlemlerinin ise olağan kapanış koşullarına tabi olarak 20 Kasım'da tamamlanmasının öngörüldüğü kaydedildi.
Diğer taraftan ABD Başkanı Donald Trump ve Rusya Devlet Başkanı Vladimir Putin, Çin'in Şıncın kentinde düzenlenen Asya-Pasifik Ekonomik İşbirliği (APEC) Zirvesi kapsamında bir araya geldi.
Trump, "Uzun yıllardır muhteşem bir ilişkimiz var. Birbirimizi uzun süredir tanıyoruz. Bence bundan pek çok harika şey ortaya çıkabilir ya da en azından bir başlangıç olabilir." ifadelerini kullandı. Bu gelişmelerle dün ABD'nin 10 yıllık tahvil faizi 3 baz puan düşüşle yüzde 5,07'ye inerken, yeni günde yüzde 5,06'da bulunuyor.

Analistler, enerji maliyetlerinin bir süredir yüksek seyretmesinin enflasyondaki katılığı artırdığını belirterek, bu durumun Avrupa Merkez Bankasının (ECB) aralık ayında faiz artırma ihtimalini güçlendirdiğini kaydetti.

Öte yandan yapay zeka yatırımlarının karlılığa dönüşmesine ilişkin soru işaretleri ve Nvidia'daki gelişmelerden hafta başından itibaren baskı altında olan teknoloji hisseleri, dün kayıplarının bir kısmını telafi etti. In a new Al Jazeera Originals film directed by Awad Joumaa, Israeli soldiers describe the psychological toll of the genocide in Gaza, yet many express no remorse.
Cost of War: The trauma Israeli soldiers bring home from Gaza | Al Jazeera Originals
Editor’s note: This article contains references to suicide and graphic descriptions of combat.
If you or someone you know is at risk of suicide, support is available through international crisis helplines.
Itay Sagi, a reservist in the Maglan unit, describes killing Hamas fighters inside Israel after October 7, 2023.
His grief is for his friends. Sagi wants to go back and fight. He does not mention the Palestinians killed in Gaza.
Boris Shtonda, who served with an Israeli special forces unit, lost a leg when an explosive device detonated inside a building in Gaza in November 2023, killing four of his friends.
“We lost our friends, we lost our families, we lost everything,” he says.
The Israeli soldiers in the film “Gaza Syndrome” speak of nightmares, panic, addiction and Israelis who died by suicide. They speak, too, of wanting to return to fight. In hours of testimony, the Palestinians of Gaza are almost entirely absent.
The overwhelming weight of Israel’s war has fallen on Palestinians in Gaza: their children, homes and hospitals. Israeli forces have killed at least 74,700 Palestinians, including more than 21,000 children, according to Al Jazeera reporting . In September 2025, an independent UN Commission of Inquiry concluded that Israeli authorities and security forces had committed genocide in Gaza. The soldiers in this film are part of those forces.
Guy Zaken, a military bulldozer driver, told an Israeli parliamentary committee that soldiers had to “run over “‘terrorists’, dead and alive, in the hundreds”. His co-driver, Eliran Mizrahi, spent 186 days in Gaza demolishing homes and died by suicide two days before he was due to return. “He got out of Gaza, but Gaza did not get out of him,” his mother told CNN.
The question is not whether the Israeli soldiers’ psychological injuries are real. It is what psychological injury means when it is joined to denial, impunity and the absence of remorse.
In The Wretched of the Earth, the mid-20th century psychiatrist and political philosopher Frantz Fanon observed that colonial violence inflicts severe psychiatric trauma on both the colonised and the perpetrators. When soldiers carry out systematic destruction and violence, the psychological toll cannot be separated from the political structure that enables and ignores it.
An Al Jazeera Investigative Unit examination of more than 2,500 Israeli soldiers’ social media accounts documented wanton destruction, abuse of detainees, and the use of Palestinian civilians as human shields.
The scale of the psychological crisis is growing. Nearly 30,000 Israeli soldiers and security personnel wounded since October 7 have entered the Defence Ministry’s rehabilitation system, the ministry said in October.
About 63 percent have psychological injuries, with thousands formally diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and acute stress reactions following prolonged combat exposure. The Israeli army says 22 soldiers died by suicide in 2025, one more than in 2024, up from 17 in 2023. An Israeli parliament Research and Information Center report recorded 279 suicide attempts between January 2024 and July 2025. Combat soldiers accounted for 78 percent of the deaths by suicide in 2024.
Mohanad Mustafa, a scholar of Israeli society, told Al Jazeera Israel faces “a psychological crisis among thousands of soldiers, but no moral crisis”.
He says many soldiers feel no remorse for violations of international law. “This indicates a very significant moral decline in Israeli society.”
Israel’s public culture has helped make that denial possible. Oren Ziv, an Israeli journalist with +972 Magazine, says soldiers he interviewed described “an atmosphere of revenge, that everything is allowed”. They could shoot if they saw movement, he says, or if they were bored, and “nobody will investigate it”.
Daniel Bar-Tal, a political psychologist, says soldiers in Gaza still confront Palestinian suffering “to some extent”, even when they deny it or refuse to see it.
This suppressed awareness, he said, creates a quiet, internal fracture, a psychological burden that deepens precisely because the trauma cannot be fully acknowledged or resolved without confronting the suffering of those they harmed.
Ashira Darwish, a Palestinian trauma therapist and survivor of severe trauma and torture who created Active Meditation to heal from full-body paralysis, believes Israeli soldiers can enter Gaza, shoot children and burn homes only by suppressing their own humanity. She and other trauma experts emphasise that returning reservists undergo a severe psychological transition when re-entering civilian life after engaging in continuous combat.
“Someone who can exterminate an entire people while sitting there laughing will carry a psychological impact.”
Darwish describes reservists returning from Gaza to a hospital, office or school within a week or two. She warns of anger, substance addiction, domestic conflict, and sudden outbursts of violence as untreated combat trauma manifests in everyday interactions. “Where are they supposed to go with everything they have done?”
Israel’s Observatory on Femicide recorded 34 femicides in 2025, a 48 percent rise from 23 in 2024. Firearms were the most common weapon for the first time. Women’s groups warned early in the war that combat trauma and expanded access to guns could heighten the risk of domestic violence. There is no official data proving that returning soldiers caused the rise, and the Observatory found no link between licenced guns and femicide. The warning is about a society saturated with weapons, fear and impunity, not a claim that every soldier becomes violent at home.
In Qusra, a Palestinian village south of Nablus in the occupied West Bank, the film finds the other end of that impunity. Abdul Azim al-Wadi, a former head of the village council, says Israeli settlers killed his brother Ibrahim and nephew Ahmad, shot two of his sons and burned his son’s and daughter’s homes.
“The occupation army is the continuation of the settlers’ attacks,” he says. “They play the role together.”
Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank are illegal under international law.
The same impunity is visible in Gaza. In NAZA, a documentary built on anonymous testimony from Israeli soldiers and intelligence personnel, sources describe civilian deaths factored into military decisions and targets watched inside their homes. The Israeli army called NAZA a “manipulative depiction of reality”.
In March, Israel dropped charges against five soldiers accused of sexually abusing a Palestinian detainee at the Sde Teiman detention facility.
A few do not accept the orders to serve in the army. Itamar Greenberg chose military prison over conscription. Iddo Elam said: “I do not want to hold a weapon towards innocent people.”
Their refusal matters because it shows the violence is not inevitable, and neither is the story Israel tells about it.
Bar-Tal offers his country a choice: “Cut the violence or cut the narrative.”
